absorptive
adjective
uk
/əbˈzɔːp.tɪv/ us
/əbˈzɔːrp.tɪv/
Add to word list Add to word list
able to take liquids or other substances in through a surface and to hold them:
The compound is formed so that it can enable uptake by absorptive cells.
the absorptive surfaces of the small intestine
Synonym
absorbent
able to be absorbed (= taken in and held or used), for example by the skin or the body:
The small molecules of goat's milk make it highly absorptive when rubbed into the skin.
absorptive vitamins and minerals
More examplesFewer examples
  • Because of its absorptive properties, tapioca flour is often used as a thickening agent in recipes.
  • A physical obstruction can be caused by matter attached to the absorptive layer of the bowel wall.
  • Compression garments and absorptive pads are applied for the immediate postoperative period.
  • Acoustic problems might be caused by a ceiling that's too high or absorptive to bounce the laughter around.
  • Acai is rich in a highly absorptive form of calcium.
